tactics.name: Observed Asset
tactics.summary: This Category contains different types of Asset which can be observed as part of a potential incident

tactics.name: Observed Asset Descriptors
tactics.summary: This Category contains different ways to describe an Asset's features or settings

tactics.name: Asset Identity Descriptors
tactics.summary: This Category contains ways to document the Identity presented as operating an Asset

tactics.name: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content
tactics.summary: This Category contains actions which relate to Publications, Assets, or Content

tactics.name: Actions Available to Platforms
tactics.summary: This Category contains actions which are available only to Platforms

tactics.name: Offline Actions
tactics.summary: This Category contains actions which are available offline

tactics.name: Publication Details
tactics.summary: This Category contains information about an online publication

tactics.name: Content Origin
tactics.summary: This Category contains infomation about the origin of content

tactics.name: Narrative Details
tactics.summary: This Category contains different types of narrative information

tactics.name: Content Effect
tactics.summary: This Category contains different impacts content can have

techniques.name: User Asset
techniques.summary: This Category contains different types of user which can take action online

techniques.name: Account Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset is a user account

techniques.name: Admin Account Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset is an administrator account

techniques.name: Unauthenticated Account Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset is an unauthenticated / guest account on a Platform which does not mandate account creation to take actions on it

techniques.name: Community Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset is an online community in which users can interact with each other

techniques.name: Online Community Group
techniques.summary: The Asset is a 'group' created using a Platform's native features (e.g. Facebook Group)

techniques.name: Online Community Page
techniques.summary: The Asset is a 'page' created using a Platform's native features (e.g. Facebook Page)

techniques.name: Chat Community Server
techniques.summary: The Asset is a collection of chat rooms and/or chat broadcast groups organised into a server (e.g. a Discord or Slack server)

techniques.name: Chat Room
techniques.summary: The Asset is a closed group where three or more users can send messages to each other

techniques.name: Chat Broadcast Group
techniques.summary: The Asset is a closed group where 'administrators' can send messages to a community who may react to, comment on, or forward the messages

techniques.name: Community Sub-Forum
techniques.summary: The Asset is a sub-forum on a community forum platform (e.g. a Subreddit)

techniques.name: Online Game Session
techniques.summary: The Asset is a session for an online game (e.g. a Roblox or Minecraft server)

techniques.name: Community Hosting Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Platform which is primarily designed for users to interact with each other as part of a community

techniques.name: Social Media Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Social Media Platform (e.g. Facebook, Instagram)

techniques.name: Chat Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Chat Platform (e.g. Whastapp, Discord)

techniques.name: Microblogging Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Microblogging Platform (e.g. Twitter, TikTok, BlueSky)

techniques.name: Legacy Online Forum Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is an old-school forum (e.g. Something Awful, War Thunder)

techniques.name: Community Forum Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is an Online Community Forum (e.g. Reddit)

techniques.name: Image Board Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is an Image Board Platform (e.g. 4chan)

techniques.name: Question and Answer Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Q&A Platform (e.g. Quora)

techniques.name: Online Game Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is an Online Game Platform (e.g. Roblox, Minecraft)

techniques.name: Dating Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Dating Platform (e.g. Tinder, Grindr)

techniques.name: Content Hosting Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Platform which is primarily designed for users to upload and consume content

techniques.name: Website Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset is a collection of associated webpages under a single domain

techniques.name: Paste Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Platform designed for sharing plaintext (e.g. Pastebin)

techniques.name: Video Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Platform designed for publishing and viewing video-based content (e.g. YouTube, Vimeo)

techniques.name: Audio Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Platform designed for publishing and listening to audio-based content (e.g. Spotify, Soundcloud, PodBean)

techniques.name: Live Streaming Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Platform designed for users to stream live content to their audience (e.g. Twitch, Kick)

techniques.name: Software Delivery Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Platform designed for publishing and downloading software (e.g. Apple App Store, Google Play Store, Steam)

techniques.name: File Hosting Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Platform designed for hosting and sharing files online (e.g. Google Drive, Dropbox)

techniques.name: Wiki Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Platform designed for online knowledge management (e.g. Wikipedia)

techniques.name: Content Subscription Service Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Platform designed for allowing users to charge a subscription for content, access, or other benefits (e.g. Patreon, OnlyFans)

techniques.name: Blog Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset is a blog in which people post typically informal articles

techniques.name: Digital Service Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Platform which is primarily designed to provide a digital service to their users

techniques.name: Blog Hosting Service Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Platform which hosts Blogs (e.g. Medium, Substack)

techniques.name: Website Hosting Service Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Platform which hosts Websites (e.g. Webflow, Weebly, Wix)

techniques.name: Email Service Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Platform which provides Email service (e.g. GMail, Proton Mail, Microsoft Office)

techniques.name: Link Shortening Service Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Link Shortening Service provder (e.g. Bitly, TinyURL)

techniques.name: Online Advertising Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is an Online Advertising platform (e.g. Meta Ads, Google Ads, Amazon Ads)

techniques.name: Search Engine Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is a Search Engine Platform (e.g. Google, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia)

techniques.name: AI LLM Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is an AI LLM provider (e.g. LeChat, Claude, Gemini)

techniques.name: AI Media Platform
techniques.summary: The Asset is an AI Media generator (e.g. Midjourney, DALL-E, Gemini)

techniques.name: Asset Configuration
techniques.summary: This Category contains ways to describe how an Asset has been configured

techniques.name: Verified Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset displays an indicator that it has been verified by the Platform it operates on

techniques.name: Lookalike Asset ID
techniques.summary: The Asset has an identifier (e.g. account handle) which is visually similar to another asset's identifier

techniques.name: Lookalike Domain
techniques.summary: The observed Platform has a domain which is visually similar to another Platform's domain (AKA typosquat)

techniques.name: Asset Description
techniques.summary: This Category contains ways to describe how an Asset has described itself (e.g. a User or Community's biography field, a Platform's 'About us' page)

techniques.name: Asset Imagery
techniques.summary: This Category contains ways to describe the imagery with which an Asset has been configured

techniques.name: Copied Asset Imagery
techniques.summary: The Asset uses imagery which is the same as imagery already used by another Asset

techniques.name: Mimicked Asset Imagery
techniques.summary: The Asset uses imagery which is visually similar (but not the same as) imagery already used by another Asset (e.g. mimicking colour scheme, typography)

techniques.name: Animal Profile Picture
techniques.summary: The User has an animal set as their profile picture

techniques.name: Scenery Profile Picture
techniques.summary: The User has scenery set as their profile picture

techniques.name: Illustrated Character Profile Picture
techniques.summary: The User has an illustrated character (e.g. Anime, Manga, Cartoon) set as their profile picture

techniques.name: Attractive Person Profile Picture
techniques.summary: The User has an attractive person set as their profile picture

techniques.name: Platform Capability
techniques.summary: This Category contains ways to document different Capabilities a Platform may have

techniques.name: Payment Processing Capability
techniques.summary: The Platform has the capability to proccess one time payments

techniques.name: Subscription Processing Capability
techniques.summary: The Platform has the capability to process payments on a recurring, automated basis

techniques.name: Email Service Capability
techniques.summary: The Platform has the capability to send and recieve emails

techniques.name: Encrypted Communication Capability
techniques.summary: Communications sent on this platform are encrypted

techniques.name: Asset Gating
techniques.summary: This Category contains ways to describe how access to an Asset is gated

techniques.name: Gated Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset prevents access to it in some way (i.e. it is 'gated')

techniques.name: Invite Gated Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset cannot be accessed by users unless the user is invited to access it

techniques.name: Approval Gated Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset cannot be accessed by users unless they use a Platform's feature to request access to it, and that request is approved

techniques.name: Geoblocked Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset is configured to prevent access to users from specified locations

techniques.name: Paid Access Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset cannot be accessed by users unless they make a one time payment

techniques.name: Subscription Access Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset cannot be accessed by users unless they make a recurring subscription payment

techniques.name: Asset Acquisition
techniques.summary: This Category contains ways to describe how an actor acquired an Asset

techniques.name: Newly Created Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset was created as part of the observed incident

techniques.name: Pre-Existing Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset was created before the observed incident

techniques.name: Asset Activated after Period of Dormancy
techniques.summary: The Asset was took part in the observed incident after a period of dormancy

techniques.name: Freely Created Asset
techniques.summary: The Platform the Asset was created on did not charge for creation

techniques.name: Paid Created Asset
techniques.summary: The Platform the Asset was created on charged for its creation

techniques.name: Bulk Created Asset
techniques.summary: The Asset was created in bulk alongside other Assets

techniques.name: Purchased Existing Asset
techniques.summary: The actor acquired the Asset by purchasing it from another individual or institution

techniques.name: Rented Existing Asset
techniques.summary: The actor acquired the Asset by renting it another individual or institution

techniques.name: Compromised Existing Asset
techniques.summary: The actor acquired the Asset by compromising another individual or institution's Asset

techniques.name: Asset Presented Identity
techniques.summary: This Category contains different ways to document the validity of the presented identity of the individual or institution operating the Asset

techniques.name: Asset Presents Anonymous Identity
techniques.summary: The Asset is not presenting an identity (i.e. the individual or institution operating the asset is choosing to not disclose who they are)

techniques.name: Asset Presents Legitimate Identity of Asset Operator
techniques.summary: The Identity presetned by the Asset is authentic (i.e. the individual or institution operating the asset is who the Asset claims it to be)

techniques.name: Asset Presents Nonexistent Identity
techniques.summary: The Identity presented by the Asset is an individual or institution which doesn't exist

techniques.name: Asset Presents Impersonation of Another Identity
techniques.summary: The Identity presented by the Asset is an impersonation of another individual or institution (i.e. it claims to be operated by someone, but it is actually operated by someone else)

techniques.name: Asset Presents Parody of Another Identity
techniques.summary: The Identity presented by the Asset is a disclosed parody of an individual or institution

techniques.name: Asset's Previous Identity Maintained after Acquisition
techniques.summary: The Identity presented by the Asset has stayed the same even though the actor operating the asset changed

techniques.name: Asset Presents New Identity
techniques.summary: The Identity which is being presented by the Asset has changed (e.g. it previously claimed it was operated by someone, now it claims it's being operated by someone else)

techniques.name: Individual Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset is an individual

techniques.name: Local Individual Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as an individual local to a given location

techniques.name: Journalist Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as a journalist

techniques.name: Activist Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as an activist

techniques.name: Hacktivist Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as a hacktivist

techniques.name: Military Personnel Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as a member of the military

techniques.name: Recruiter Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as a recruiter

techniques.name: Researcher Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as a researcher

techniques.name: Expert Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as an expert on a given topic area

techniques.name: Romantic Suitor Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as an individual persuing a romantic or physical relationship

techniques.name: Party Official Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as an individual representing a political party

techniques.name: Government Official Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as an indiviaul serving as a member of the governing party of a country

techniques.name: Government Employee Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as an individual employed to work as part of the government

techniques.name: Law Enforcement Officer Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as a member of law enforcement in a country

techniques.name: Sex Worker Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as a sex worker

techniques.name: Institutional Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset is an institution

techniques.name: Local Institution Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as in institution local to a given location

techniques.name: News Outlet Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as a news outlet

techniques.name: Fact Checking Organisation Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as a fact checking organisation

techniques.name: Think Tank Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as a think tank

techniques.name: Business Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as business

techniques.name: Government Institution Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as government or government body

techniques.name: NGO Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as non-govermental organisation, non-profit, or other volunteer organisation

techniques.name: Social Cause Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as a collective campaigning for a social cause

techniques.name: Adult Entertainment Outlet Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset presents itself as a provider of adult entertainment (e.g. Pornography)

techniques.name: Asset Role Validity
techniques.summary: This Category contains ways to document whether the Identity has legitimate claim to the Role they present themselves as having

techniques.name: Identity Has Legitimate Claim to Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset has legitimate claim to the Role they present themselves as having

techniques.name: Identity Does Not Have Legitimate Claim to Role
techniques.summary: The Identity presented as operating the asset does not have legitimate claim to the Role they present themselves as having

techniques.name: Use of Automation
techniques.summary: This Category contains ways to document the use of automation and its disclosure in an asset

techniques.name: Asset Uses and Discloses Automation
techniques.summary: The Asset uses automation to operate online, and discloses the use of automation

techniques.name: Asset Uses Automation without Disclosure
techniques.summary: The Asset uses automation to operate online, and does not disclose the use of automation

techniques.name: Publish Online Publication
techniques.summary: This Cateogry contains Actions related to publishing a Publication
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Publish
techniques.summary: Publish a post to an online community or group
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Send
techniques.summary: Send a message or email to a closed messaging group or service
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Conduct
techniques.summary: Conduct a live stream or call to a public or private audience
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Upload
techniques.summary: Upload a file to a platform
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Comment
techniques.summary: Comment on another existing Publication
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Submit
techniques.summary: Submit a report or search to a platform
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Amplify Online Publication
techniques.summary: This Cateogry contains Actions related to amplifying a Publication
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Repost
techniques.summary: Use a platform’s “Repost” feature
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Emote React
techniques.summary: Use a platform’s “Emote React” feature
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Forward
techniques.summary: Use a platform’s “Forward” feature
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Interact with Community or User
techniques.summary: This Category contains Actions taken on Users or Communities on Platforms
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Request Connection with Asset
techniques.summary: Use a platform’s feature to request a connection with another asset (sometimes called “Friending” or “Adding)
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Connect with Asset
techniques.summary: Use a platform’s feature to make a connection with another account (sometimes called Accepting, Approving or Confirming a Friend Request)
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Follow Asset
techniques.summary: Use a platform’s feature to follow another asset
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Join Community
techniques.summary: Use a platform’s feature to join a community on the platform
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Add Asset to Community
techniques.summary: Use a platform’s feature to add another asset to a community on the platform
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Block Asset
techniques.summary: Use a platform’s feature to “Block” another asset
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Acquire Content
techniques.summary: This Category contains methods of acquiring Content
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Produce
techniques.summary: Produce text, image, video, or audio content
techniques.tactic: Interact with Publication, Asset, or Content

techniques.name: Platform Curation Actions
techniques.summary: This Category contains actions taken by a Platform to curate their Users' experience

techniques.name: Host
techniques.summary: Host publications, content, users, or communities on a platform

techniques.name: Promote
techniques.summary: A platform feature promotes a publication or piece of content

techniques.name: Deliver
techniques.summary: A platform delivers search results or an advertisement

techniques.name: Platform Prompting Action
techniques.summary: This Category contains actions taken by a Platform to prompt a User to take an action

techniques.name: Suggest Action
techniques.summary: A platform feature suggests an action to its user

techniques.name: Enable Action
techniques.summary: A platform feature enables its user to take an action

techniques.name: Platform Takes Moderation Action
techniques.summary: This Category contains moderation actions available to Platforms

techniques.name: Platform Suppresses Algorithmic Reach
techniques.summary: A platform suppresses the algorithmic reach of a publication, user, or community on its platform

techniques.name: Platform Suppresses Search Results
techniques.summary: A platform suppresses search results from being delivered to a user of its platform

techniques.name: Platform Removes Publication from Platform
techniques.summary: A platform removes a publication from its platform

techniques.name: Platform Applies Disclaimer
techniques.summary: A platform applies a disclaimer to a publication, user, or community on its platform

techniques.name: Platform Suspends Asset
techniques.summary: A platform suspends an asset from its platform

techniques.name: Platform Failure to Take Action
techniques.summary: This Category contains ways to document a Platform's failure to take action on harmful or infringing content

techniques.name: Platform Fails to Address Asset with Repeat Infringements
techniques.summary: A platform takes no moderation action against an asset with repeat infringements

techniques.name: Platform Fails to Reverse Erroneous Moderation Action
techniques.summary: A platform fails to reverse moderation action it took erroneously (e.g. unjustified or accidental moderation)

techniques.name: Platform Fails to Act on Report in Timely Manner
techniques.summary: A report submitted to a platform is not acted upon in a reasonable amount of time

techniques.name: Platform Denies Infringement is Infringing
techniques.summary: A platform denies that an infringing user, community, publication, or piece of content is infringing

techniques.name: Issue with Platform Moderation Action
techniques.summary: This Category contains ways to describe issues with moderation actions taken by a Platform

techniques.name: Platform Fails to Provide Clear Reason for Moderation Decision
techniques.summary: A platform took moderation action without providing a clear reason

techniques.name: Platform Fails to Adequately Communicate Moderation Decision
techniques.summary: A platform took moderation action without adequately communicating their decision

techniques.name: Platform Fails to Disclose Use of Automation in Moderation Decision
techniques.summary: A platform took automated moderation action without disclosing the use of automation

techniques.name: Platform Fails to Provide Method to Challenge Moderation Decision
techniques.summary: A platform took moderation and did not provide a method to challenge the moderation action

techniques.name: Platform Fails to Meet Legal Standards for Method to Challenge Moderation Decision
techniques.summary: The method a platform provides to challenge a moderation decision fails to meet legal standards

techniques.name: Offline Harm
techniques.summary: This Category contains types of offline harm

techniques.name: Physical Violence
techniques.summary: An individual or group has conducted physical violence on another individual or group

techniques.name: Physical Sexual Violence
techniques.summary: An individual or group has conducted physical sexual violence on another individual or group

techniques.name: Publication Type
techniques.summary: This Category contains different things which can be published online, like posts, streams, messages, and more

techniques.name: Post
techniques.summary: A Post is static content which is typically published to a broad community of users who can view its contents

techniques.name: Message
techniques.summary: A Message is static content which is typically sent to a closed community in a group chat or server, or an individual over direct messaging

techniques.name: Email
techniques.summary: An Email is static content which is typically sent to the private inbox of one or more recipients

techniques.name: Call
techniques.summary: A Call is a live, private communication between two or more participants in video or audio format

techniques.name: Stream
techniques.summary: A Stream is a live broadcast typically conducted to a broad community of users, who can comment in reaction to events

techniques.name: File
techniques.summary: A File is a container for digital information on a device

techniques.name: Report of Infraction
techniques.summary: A Report of Infraction is submitted by using a platform’s reporting feature to flag Material or an Asset which goes against the platform’s stated policy, or local laws

techniques.name: Search
techniques.summary: A Search is submitted by using a platform’s search feature to return Material or an Asset on the platform

techniques.name: Search Results
techniques.summary: Search Resuts are a list of items delivered by a Platform when after a user submits a search to them

techniques.name: Advertisement
techniques.summary: An Advertisement is delivered by a Platform to its users

techniques.name: Content Format
techniques.summary: This Category contains different ways content can be formatted; Text, Audio, Video, or Image

techniques.name: Text Content
techniques.summary: Content which takes the form of text

techniques.name: Templated Text
techniques.summary: Text which has been produced following a template

techniques.name: Image Content
techniques.summary: Content which takes the form of an image

techniques.name: Evidence Collage
techniques.summary: An image which collates different material into a collage of evidence to support a narrative or claim

techniques.name: Text Presented in Image Format
techniques.summary: An image file which has been produced predominantly to house text content e.g. to avoid text-based moderation

techniques.name: Video Content
techniques.summary: Content which takes the form of a video

techniques.name: Vertical Video
techniques.summary: A video produced in the vertical format, a form factor optimised for mobile viewing

techniques.name: Horizontal Video
techniques.summary: A video produced in the horizontal format, a form factor optimised for desktop, laptop, or televisual viewing

techniques.name: Subtitled Speech
techniques.summary: Subtitled speech on video content

techniques.name: Audio Content
techniques.summary: Content which takes the form of audio

techniques.name: Music
techniques.summary: Audio in the form of music

techniques.name: Content Style
techniques.summary: This Category contains different ways a publication or a piece of content can be styled

techniques.name: News Report
techniques.summary: Content has been styled as a news report

techniques.name: Opinion Piece
techniques.summary: Content has been styled as an opinion piece

techniques.name: Academic Research Report
techniques.summary: Content has been styled as an academic research report

techniques.name: Fact Check
techniques.summary: Content has been styled as a fact check

techniques.name: Impersonated Content
techniques.summary: Content has been produced in such a way that it impersonates publications or content produced by another individual or institution

techniques.name: Document
techniques.summary: Content has been styled in the format of a document

techniques.name: Book
techniques.summary: Content has been styled in the form of a book

techniques.name: Podcast Episode
techniques.summary: Content has been produced in the format of a podcast episode

techniques.name: Content Details
techniques.summary: This Category contains different ways a piece of content can be styled

techniques.name: Content Constitutes Leak of Private Material
techniques.summary: Private materials have been non-consensually published to an audience not originally intended to have access to said materials

techniques.name: Secret Recording
techniques.summary: Audio, Video, or Image content produced without the knowledge of those recorded

techniques.name: Screen Capture
techniques.summary: An image or video produced by taking a screen capture of what was visible on a user’s device

techniques.name: Anonymised Content
techniques.summary: Content intentionally produced to anonymise individuals depicted, or to hide the identity of who produced it

techniques.name: Meme
techniques.summary: Content is styled in the form of an internet meme; content which is humorous in nature, often referentially with slight variants made by different users

techniques.name: Stock Content
techniques.summary: Audio, Video, or Image content sourced from a stock media provider, or placeholder text content

techniques.name: Language Details
techniques.summary: This Category contains details about use of language which aren’t indicative of misleading or malicious behaviour on their own, but may be useful information for making assessments about an actor

techniques.name: Translated Content
techniques.summary: Content which has been translated from one language to another

techniques.name: Non-Native Language Error
techniques.summary: A non-native language error is a mistake or oddity in use of language atypical of a native speaker

techniques.name: Coded Terminology
techniques.summary: Content makes use of coded terminology, e.g. letter replacements in words, 'algospeak', euphemisms, or dog whistles

techniques.name: Machine Translated Content
techniques.summary: Use of automation, online translation tools, AI, or other non-manual translation methods to translate material from one language to another

techniques.name: Demonstrably False Content
techniques.summary: This Category contains types of content which can be shown to have been artificially created, or content that contains information which is demonstrably incorrect

techniques.name: Statement Incorrectly Presented as Made by Individual or Institution
techniques.summary: A statement has incorrectly been presented as having been made by an individual or institution

techniques.name: Falsified Depiction of Content Amplification
techniques.summary: Image of Video content which has been created to give the false impression that another piece of content is being amplified online

techniques.name: Falsified Graffiti or Signage
techniques.summary: Image or Video content which has been edited to impose graffiti or other signage

techniques.name: Imagery Depicting Individual Edited to Introduce Sexual Material
techniques.summary: Sexual content has been edited to introduce the target individual’s visage

techniques.name: Claim to Nonexistent Physical Address
techniques.summary: An ownership or association claim is made with regards to a physical address, but the address doesn't exist

techniques.name: Incorrect Claim to Real Physical Address
techniques.summary: An ownership or association claim is made with regards to a physical address, but the address is not actually owned or associated with the claimant

techniques.name: Mislabeled Publication
techniques.summary: A Publication has not been correctly labeled in line with platform policy (e.g. an Advertisement missing a political label)

techniques.name: Action Incorrectly Presented as Taken by Individual or Institution
techniques.summary: A claim incorrectly attributes an action as having been taken by an individual or institution

techniques.name: Content Relationship to Platform Policy
techniques.summary: This Category enables documentation of whether content is aligned with a platform's stated policy

techniques.name: Content Goes Against Platform Policy
techniques.summary: Published content goes against the stated policy of the platform it was published to

techniques.name: Content Within Platform Policy
techniques.summary: Published content is within the stated policy of the platform it was published to

techniques.name: Publication Use of Platform Features
techniques.summary: This Category contains different features platforms offer which an be applied to a publication

techniques.name: Tag Geolocation
techniques.summary: Use of a Platform's feature to tag a geolocation

techniques.name: Tag Hashtag
techniques.summary: Use of a Platform's feature to tag a hashtag

techniques.name: Tag Asset
techniques.summary: Use of a Platform's feature to tag an asset

techniques.name: Publication Access Settings
techniques.summary: This Category contains different ways that access to a publication can be configured

techniques.name: Number of Times Publication can be Viewed Limited per User
techniques.summary: A post or message uses a platform's feature to limit the number of times it is able to be viewed per user (e.g. Snapchat Snaps)

techniques.name: Access to Publication Automatically Removed after Specified Time Expires
techniques.summary: A post, message or file uses a platform's feature to automatically remove the ability to view it after a time window has expired (e.g. Instagram Stories)

techniques.name: Ability to View Publication Restricted to Specified Audience within Platform
techniques.summary: A post, stream, or file which would otherwise be accessible to a broad group of users (per the platform's default functionality) has been configured to be viewable only to a specified group by the publishing asset

techniques.name: Ability to Comment on Publication Restricted to Specified Audience within Platform
techniques.summary: A post, stream, or file which would otherwise be accessible to a broad group of users (per the platform's default functionality) has been configured to be commentable to a specified group by the publishing asset

techniques.name: Ability to Comment on Publication Disabled for All Users within Platform
techniques.summary: A post, stream, message, or file has had the platform's default comment functionality turned off for all platform users

techniques.name: AI-Generated Content
techniques.summary: Content was generated using AI

techniques.name: Deepfake Impersonation
techniques.summary: AI was used to generate a deepfake impersonation of an individual

techniques.name: Sexual Deepfake Impersonation
techniques.summary: AI was used to generate a deepfake impersonation of an individual which depicts them sexually

techniques.name: AI-Nudified Imagery
techniques.summary: AI was used to produce an undressed (‘nudified’) version of existing media

techniques.name: Private Materials
techniques.summary: This Category contains different types of content typically intended for a private audience

techniques.name: Personally Identifiable Information
techniques.summary: Content contains personally identifiable information (or “PII”) about a person or institution, such as their name, social accounts, physical address, contact details, information about their employer, or their friends or family

techniques.name: Private Intimate Imagery
techniques.summary: Content is private intimate imagery; imagery which depicts an individual in a state of undress, engaging in sexual activity, or in other intimate situations where there is a reasonable expectation of privacy

techniques.name: Internal Communications
techniques.summary: Content is internal communications originally intended to be kept private by the communicating party

techniques.name: Internal Document
techniques.summary: Content is an internal document originally intended to be kept private by the party who created it

techniques.name: Internal Contacts List
techniques.summary: Content is an internal list of people or institutions, and their contact details

techniques.name: Asset Login Credentials
techniques.summary: Content is login credentials for an online asset (e.g. an account)

techniques.name: Edited Content
techniques.summary: Content has been edited without disclosure

techniques.name: Clipped Content
techniques.summary: Content was clipped from a longer piece of Audio or Video Content without disclosure

techniques.name: Cropped Content
techniques.summary: Image or Video Content has been edited to zoom in on part of the visuals without disclosure

techniques.name: Playback Speed Altered
techniques.summary: Audio or Video Content has had its playback speed edited without disclosure

techniques.name: Source Removed from Content
techniques.summary: Content was edited in such a way that its original source has been removed or obscured without disclosure

techniques.name: AI-Edited Content
techniques.summary: AI has been used to edit existing content

techniques.name: Content Verifiability
techniques.summary: This Category contains items which can be used to document the degree to which information can be independently verified or validated

techniques.name: Information is Verified
techniques.summary: Information presented by the actor has been independently confirmed by the analyst through credible fact-checking

techniques.name: Information is False
techniques.summary: Information presented by the actor has been confirmed to be false by the analyst through credible fact-checking

techniques.name: Information is Unverifiable
techniques.summary: Information presented by the actor cannot be confirmed or refuted by the analyst due to a lack of accessible, credible evidence

techniques.name: Information is Misleading
techniques.summary: Information presented by the actor contains some accurate or verifiable information, but is presented in a misleading way

techniques.name: Content Produced as Satire
techniques.summary: Content was created for humor or commentary, not to convey factual information

techniques.name: Content Previously Fact Checked
techniques.summary: Content has been identified which was previously addressed by Fact Checkers

techniques.name: Claim Previously Fact Checked
techniques.summary: A claim has been identified which was previously addressed by Fact Checkers

techniques.name: Reframe Context
techniques.summary: Information presented outside of its original context in such a way that reframes its meaning or implications

techniques.name: Incorrect Subtitled Speech Reframes Context
techniques.summary: Incorrect translation of subtitled speech giving a false impression of what was being said

techniques.name: Edits Made to News Report which Reframe Context
techniques.summary: A report published by a legitimate news outlet has been edited to change what was reported

techniques.name: Historic Content Incorrectly Presented as Current
techniques.summary: Content depicting previously occurring events presented as depicting a recent or ongoing event

techniques.name: Content Incorrectly Presented as Depicting Another Location
techniques.summary: Content depicting one location presented as if it depicts a different location

techniques.name: Video Game Content Incorrectly Presented as Depicting Reality
techniques.summary: Footage from video games presented as authentic, real-world material

techniques.name: AI-Generated Content Incorrectly Presented as Depicting Reality
techniques.summary: Images, videos, or audio generated using AI presented as authentic, real-world material

techniques.name: Context Reframed by Edits to Media
techniques.summary: Altered or manipulated content is presented as unedited and authentic

techniques.name: Statement Reframed by Removal from Context
techniques.summary: A statement made by an individual or institution has been taken out of context, which reframes its meaning or interpretation

techniques.name: Entertainment Media Content Incorrectly Presented as Depicting Reality
techniques.summary: Clips or stills from staged movies, series, or other staged performances are shared as authentic, non-staged depiction of real-world events

techniques.name: Content Originally Produced as Satire Presented as Not Satire
techniques.summary: Genuine satire is shared as though it were factual reporting

techniques.name: Issues with Cited Academic Research
techniques.summary: Narrative provides a citation to academic research which has issues impacting its legitimacy

techniques.name: Narrative Cites Nonexistent Academic Research
techniques.summary: Narrative provides a citation to academic research which does not exist to support a claim

techniques.name: Narrative Misrepresents Findings of Cited Academic Research
techniques.summary: Narrative misrepresents the findings of cited academic research to support a claim

techniques.name: Narrative Cites Retracted Academic Research
techniques.summary: Narrative supports a claim by citing academic research which has been retracted

techniques.name: Narrative Cites Academic Research not Peer Reviewed
techniques.summary: Narrative does not disclose that it cites academic research which has not been peer reviewed to support a claim

techniques.name: Issues with Presented Statistical Evidence
techniques.summary: A claim is presented alongside statistics which have validity issues

techniques.name: Narrative Presents Fabricated Statistics as Genuine Data
techniques.summary: A claim is presented alongside statistics which were not generated using real data points, but presented as legitimate statistics grounded in research

techniques.name: Narrative Uses Selective Statistics to Support Claim
techniques.summary: Content presents a selective subset of data which produces beneficial statistics to support a claim

techniques.name: Narrative Uses Misinterpreted Statistics to Support Claim
techniques.summary: Narrative uses real statistics in support of a claim, but presents an incorrect interpretation of their meaning

techniques.name: Narrative Uses Misleading Data Visualisation
techniques.summary: Narrative presents a data visualisation (such as a bar, line, or pie chart) which misrepresents data in support of a claim

techniques.name: Issue with Content's Headline
techniques.summary: There is an issue with how a piece of content has been titled

techniques.name: Content Constitutes Clickbait
techniques.summary: Content with attention-grabbing, knowledge gap titles to attract attention and encourage a view

techniques.name: Rhetorical Device
techniques.summary: This Category contains rhetorical devices or fallacies which can mislead

techniques.name: Narrative Ties In to Current Events
techniques.summary: A narrative builds upon or otherwise ties in to events or narratives which are currently or recently within the public conversation or sphere of focus

techniques.name: Narrative Uses False Cause
techniques.summary: False cause is the fallacy of assuming that one event causes another simply because the two occur together or in sequence

techniques.name: Narrative Uses Whataboutism
techniques.summary: Whataboutism is a rhetorical device in which someone avoids addressing an argument by diverting attention to a different or unrelated issue

techniques.name: Narrative Uses Cherry Picking
techniques.summary: Cherry-picking refers to selectively presenting evidence that supports a claim while ignoring evidence that challenges it

techniques.name: Narrative Uses Anecdote
techniques.summary: Anecdotes are the use of evidence in the form of personal experience or an isolated case, possibly rumour or hearsay, most often to discredit statistics

techniques.name: Narrative Uses Strawman
techniques.summary: Strawman is a rhetorical device in which someone misrepresents or exaggerates another person’s argument to make it easier to attack or refute

techniques.name: Narrative Uses Leading Question
techniques.summary: Leading questions are a manipulative questioning technique where the phrasing or sequence of questions subtly steers the respondent toward a predetermined conclusion

techniques.name: Narrative Uses Appeal to Emotion
techniques.summary: Appeal to emotion is a persuasive tactic that uses emotionally charged language to provoke strong feelings instead of presenting logical evidence

techniques.name: Narrative Uses Exaggeration
techniques.summary: Exaggeration is the act of overstating or amplifying facts, qualities, or events to make them seem more significant or dramatic than they really are

techniques.name: Content Sourcing Details
techniques.summary: This Category contains different sourcing claims for a piece of content

techniques.name: Incorrect Content Source Presented
techniques.summary: An incorrect source is presented as having produced a piece of content

techniques.name: Content Presented as Produced by Third Party
techniques.summary: A piece of content is framed as having been produced by a third party

techniques.name: Content Presented as Produced by Actor
techniques.summary: A piece of content is framed as having been produced by the actor who published the content

techniques.name: Source Embedded in Media
techniques.summary: Image or video content contains sourcing embedded within the it (e.g. a visual overlay providing the source)

techniques.name: Content Algorithmic Optimisation
techniques.summary: This Category contains different ways content can be optimised for performance in platforms' algorithms

techniques.name: Platform Recommendation Algorithm Optimised Content
techniques.summary: Content has been intentionally produced in such a way that it optimises how a platform's content recommendation algorithm favours it in promoting it to platform users

techniques.name: Search Engine Optimised Content
techniques.summary: Content has been intentionally produced in such a way that it optimises its ranking in search results provided by search engine platforms

techniques.name: Content Contains Link
techniques.summary: This Category contains different ways content can link to other online content or assets

techniques.name: Content Contains Disguised Link
techniques.summary: Content links out to another online asset or material using a link which has been disguised using a hyperlink to look it links to something else

techniques.name: Content Contains Shortened Link
techniques.summary: Content links out to another online asset or material using a link which has been shortened by a link shortening service

techniques.name: Content Contains QR Code Link
techniques.summary: Content links out to another online asset or material using a QR Code

techniques.name: Content Contains Embedded Link
techniques.summary: Content uses a platform's native embedding feature to link to another asset or material, such as a quote post on X/Twitter, or a video end screen on YouTube

techniques.name: Content Action
techniques.summary: This Category contains different actions which can be taken by a piece of content

techniques.name: Content Threatens Action
techniques.summary: Content includes the threat of taking a specific action

techniques.name: Content Encourages Action
techniques.summary: Content includes the encourages another user to take a specific action

techniques.name: Content Contains Instructions for Action
techniques.summary: Content includes instructions on how to take a specific action

techniques.name: Content Solicits Action
techniques.summary: Content includes a request for another user to take a specific action

techniques.name: Content Depicts Offline Harm
techniques.summary: Content depicts an offline harm

techniques.name: Harmful Content
techniques.summary: Content is harmful in nature

techniques.name: Content Constitutes Unsolicited Sexual Imagery
techniques.summary: Content is sexual in nature, and has been delivered unsolicited to an audience (AKA “cyberflashing”)

techniques.name: Content Constitutes Unsolicited Request for Sexual Imagery
techniques.summary: Content constitutes an unsolicited request for sexual imagery from an individual

techniques.name: Content Constitutes Voyeuristic Content
techniques.summary: Image or Video content secretively taken of another individual for sexual purpose

techniques.name: Content Constitutes CSAM
techniques.summary: Content is media which show sexual abuse or exploitation of a child

techniques.name: Content Constitutes Sextortion
techniques.summary: Content extorts an individual with threat of non-consensual publication of sexual material depicting the target

techniques.name: Content Constitutes Abusive Content
techniques.summary: Content is targeted negative messaging, unwanted by the recipient

techniques.name: Content Constitutes Discriminatory Content
techniques.summary: Content is harmful or negative messaging that perpetuates stereotypes, biases, or prejudices based on a single personal characteristic such as sexual orientation, gender, race, religion, disability, or other legally protected social identities or attributes.

techniques.name: Content Constitutes Intersectional Discriminatory Content
techniques.summary: Content is harmful or negative messaging that perpetuates stereotypes, biases, or prejudices based on multiple personal characteristic such as sexual orientation, gender, race, religion, disability, or other legally protected social identities or attributes.

techniques.name: Content Constitutes Eating Disorder Content
techniques.summary: Content promotes eating disorder behaviours, such as extremee weight loss, pro-anarexia or bulimia content, harmful diet and exertcise plans, or image or video content which may trigger harmful eating disorder behaviours
